steps.text: In large pot saute; the onions, garlic, and ginger in a little olive oil for about 5 minutes.

Add the water, lentils, chick peas, white kidney beans, diced tomatoes, carrots, celery, garam masala, cardamom, cayenne pepper and cumin. Bring to a boil for a few minutes then simmer for 1 to 1 1/2 hours or longer, until the lentils are soft.
Puree half the soup in a food processor or blender. Return the pureed soup to the pot, stir and enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Moroccan Lentil Soup
raw_recipe.description: This soup is deliciously spicy, completely vegetarian, has no cholesterol, and is high in protein and fiber. It is brimming with vegetables, chick peas, white beans, and red lentils, and seasoned with cardamom, garam masala, cumin, and fresh ginger.
raw_recipe.name: Moroccan Lentil Soup

review.reviewBody: This soup has an excellent Indian flavor. Some friends walked into the house just after I started to boil the soup and they commented on the wonderful aroma that filled the house! I used brown lentils instead of red, I used red kidney beans instead of cannellini (which is white kidney beans), and I diced my own carrots, tomatoes, and celery. Fresh is always better than canned! I also used bagged beans instead of canned because of the higher nutritional value bagged beans have, so I had to let the soup cook longer (I made it around 8 AM and it was ready by 9 PM. I didn't have any cardamom so I used 3/4 teaspoon of ground cinnamon and 3/4 teaspoon of ground cloves. Garam masala is a spice combo of cinnamon, cloves, and black pepper, so you don't really need more garam masala... A great taste!

I threw all ingredients into a crock pot: 1 c brown lentils, 1 chopped onion, 1/2 c chopped carrot, 2 chopped potatoes, 1 can white beans, 14 oz crushed tomatoes, 1 quart chicken stock, 1 cup water, 2 t minced garlic, 1/2 t gr ginger, 2 t. garam masala, 1/2 t cayenne, 1/2 t cumin. Set to low and cooked 12 hrs. House smells like heaven. Didn't add cardomom because I didn't have any, but I sure will next time. Thank you Grace and Mae for expanding my Meatless Monday menu!

Made in Instant Pot. I added ingredients to pot, minus the chick peas and beans. Cooked high pressure 15 minutes, and let release naturally for 15 minutes. Added peas and beans after releasing pressure, and the heat of the soup warmed them up immediately. The lentils had softened so much I didn't have to blend or puree the soup. OUTSTANDING.

This is very good as described and excellent -- IMHO - with the addition of:

1 tsp + cumin
1 tsp + chipotle (yeah, not Moroccan, but adds savoury depth)
Juice of one large lemon (and maybe some zest). Could also add orange zest.
3-4 bay leaves (while simmering)
Salt and pepper to taste

Tip: If you enjoy a more substantive, "toothy" texture:
use green lentils, as they tend to retain their integrity better than red, and 
don't necessarily blend half as recommended.

Btw - it's a BIG pot of soup. We made half the recipe and it was still plenty for 6, plus leftovers. With a salad, a great and easy dinner in a bowl.

Absolutely delicious, aromatic and brim full of exotic flavor. Made some recipe changes after reading what others had said: (1) substituted 2 tsps of the Moroccan spice blend called Ras El Hanout (McCormick Gourmet version, for what it's worth) for 1 tsp. of Garam Masala; (2) cut back the cardamom to 1 tsp; (3) used a cup and a half of carrots and a cup of celery (because why not?); (4) used 3 cups of water and 4 cups of vegetable broth instead of 6 cups water; (5) diced up some fresh cherry tomatoes and held them back until near the end; (6) after letting tomatoes cook a bit, pureed half of soup per recipe and poured it back in, then added a 10 oz package of fresh spinach and simmered for another 5 minutes or so before serving with a white wine, a fresh and fruitful Argentinian Torrontes. The results were phenomenal. Top three all-time soups!

Great vegan option that my vegan friends and my meat-eating son and husband liked. I followed the recipe with a few changes. I used 1 1/2 teaspoons of garam masala. I didn't have plain cayenne so I used chipotle. I also added a big spoonful of miso to the water to give it more body. I waited until the last half hour to add tomatoes and some salt, so that the lentils would soften more quickly. I also added an extra can of beans at the end as the other ones had turned to mush and wanted to have chunky bites. If I had Harissa paste, I would of used that (if vegan). I served it with a spinach salad and sour dour bread.

I added and sauteed only one big onion first, then added garlic, and then sauteed the carrots and celery for a while. I added 2 big ch. tomatoes instead of a can of tomatoes but held off until closer to the end because I read that tomatoes will slow down the lentils from softening. I added 1 can of drained kidney and 1 can of drained cannelini beans, in place of called for beans. I added 1 t. cumin, 1 t. grated fresh ginger, 1/2 tsp. cinnamon, 1/2 tsp. coriander, 1/4 c. cloves as my only spices. I could probably have added more of the seasonings. I added 4 C. broth and 2 C. water.

Very tasty soup, but I made a few modifications. The first modification I made was to use chicken stock instead of water. In the cooler months, I'll use a 50-50 combination of beef bone broth and water. 

The next modification was to cook the onions alone for 3 minutes, and then add the garlic and ginger for another 2 minutes. Otherwise, you're likely to burn the latter two ingredients. 

The next modification I made was to add 1t of mineralized salt, since my chicken stock is unsalted.

I found that I needed stir the soup during the simmer phase to prevent the beans from burning on the bottom of the pot, and that the cooking time was only 75 min.

Rather than pureeing half the soup, I pureed only the beans. After they've cooked, they don't require any water to puree.

I read the reviews before I made the soup. I followed Serena's suggestion and used more Moroccan spices. The rest of the recipe I made as written. I would change a few things if I make it again. I would toast the spices with the onion and garlic to bring out the oils in the spices before adding the rest of the ingredients. I would omit the celery and add spinach or other green at the end to just wilt.

Absolutely delicious! I used chicken stock- water seemed so bland. Cut cayenne in half, but doubled garam mascara made from a recipe on this site. Added extra generous portions of the veggies plus threw in a bunch of fresh spinach toward the end. I did not find it necessary to blend half the soup. I did use canned lentils. Only bean I drained were garbanzos, so maybe that is why. It was so pretty I didn't want to ruin it! Kids gave a solid 5 stars, so will make again!

This soup is delicious, a family favorite, 5 stars with mom‘s adjustments. I use chicken broth instead of water. I double the seasoning pretty much in this recipe, and add salt. I add some type of spicy sausage, so I don’t generally need to use the cayenne pepper (usually has a pretty good kick). Then, I add kale last. My family loves this soup served with naan bread.

I made it with the variation suggested by reviewer, Serena, also using chicken broth in place of water. It was a good flavor variation from my usual spices! I used one can of chick peas along with green lentils.

Starts out seeming basic and by then end Delicious. I added more vegies as others suggested and substituted vegie stock for chicken. It will be fun to play with add ons later on or not! Good just the way it is.

Very good and spicey. Enjoyed spices I have not used previously and used chicken broth for a little extra nutrition. Soup did not call for salt but I found a little sprinkle in the bowl worked great. Served it with flat bread and added a little more cumin. Perfect! Update - still enjoyed the soup however I tried a Garam masala and it was terrible. There was no aromatic aroma in the house as in the past. Where can I find a good jar?
Way too much garam masala and cardamom. I'd halve the masala, and only use a half teaspoon of cardamom. Otherwise it would have been good.
Even with the strong spices in this recipe, it still needed a lot of help to be worth a second bowl.
Loved it!
By itself, the soup is pretty bland but add some ground Italian sausage and it is perfect! Substitute a little cinnamon for the cardamom.
